title: mos.metadata.v1
description: Disc-identity record emitted by `mos metadata --json` (design: doc/research/2026-06-10-media-info-design.md). The `disc` object is THE FINGERPRINT SUBTREE: consumers hash its canonical serialization (or a class-appropriate subset, e.g. disc.toc alone for audio CDs; match policy is theirs). Identity fields are REQUIRED AND NULLABLE, never optional — a fixed key set keeps the canonical form trivial. null means the fact was unreadable or inapplicable at capture; partial readability is the normal regime, not an error. Hard failures (drive unopenable, state query failed) emit mos.error.v1 instead.

schema.description: Schema identifier. Per-document versioned — consumers dispatch on this field.

bsd_node.description: Whole-disk dev node, or null when no IOMedia child exists (media absent). Addressing/capture context, NOT part of the fingerprint subtree.

captured_at.description: Wall-clock capture time, RFC 3339 UTC with millisecond precision (same rendering as mos.probe.v0 ts). Capture context, not identity.

volume_path.description: Mount point of the disc's volume (DiskArbitration VolumePath), or null when not mounted. Unmounted is the COMMON case for UDF video discs. Mount-point bytes are environment-controlled; consumers quoting them own their own escaping.

disc.description: The fingerprint subtree. Fixed key set (additionalProperties: false + all keys required): a v1 consumer hashing the canonical serialization never sees a key this schema does not name.

profile.description: MMC current-profile code (lowercase 0xNNNN), or null when no profile was reported (drive not READY — the state core populates the profile only on READY to avoid stale-profile leakage; see mos.state.v1).

class.description: Coarse media class derived from profile by mos_profile_class(); null when profile is null or classless. Same closed set as mos.state.v1 media_class (drift-guarded in validate.py).

toc.description: READ TOC/PMA/ATIP format 0000b decode (LBA addressing), or null when the disc/drive did not answer or the reply failed the fail-closed parse (out-of-range, duplicate, or non-ascending tracks; header/descriptor mismatch — see mos_internal_toc_parse). For CDs this is THE identity primitive (MusicBrainz/CDDB ids are pure functions of these fields, computed consumer-side). A synthesized single-track DVD/BD TOC is emitted faithfully but is identity-useless — never key on it (research doc).

leadout_lba.description: Lead-out start LBA, or null when the TOC carried no lead-out descriptor — which means NO IDENTITY: do not dedup on a lead-out-less TOC. On non-CD media the whole TOC is drive-FABRICATED per spec (MMC-5 table 483 for DVD; Mt. Fuji INF-TA-1010 for BD): one data track at LBA 0 plus this lead-out. On overwritable media (DVD+RW/BD-RE) some firmwares report formatted capacity rather than written extent here — do not treat it as a precise recorded-data size; READ DISC INFORMATION is the size authority.

data.description: Q-channel control bit 2 (data track). Derived from control; carried explicitly so consumers need no bit arithmetic.

pre_emphasis.description: Audio track recorded with 50/15 us pre-emphasis (Q-channel control bit 0). Derived from control like 'data', and meaningful only on AUDIO tracks: on a data track (control bit 2 set) bit 0 is not pre-emphasis, so this is always false there. BEST-EFFORT, like the audio-ripping tools that read it from the TOC: a disc that flags pre-emphasis only in the R-W subchannel (which mos does not read) reads false here. A consumer that must be exact de-emphasizes on subchannel evidence too.

disc_info.description: READ DISC INFORMATION (0x51) decode, or null when the drive/disc did not answer (pressed DVD-ROM/BD-ROM units that reject 0x51 are normal). status 'other' is the NORMAL regime for random-access recordable media (DVD-RAM, BD-RE) — not an anomaly.

status.description: Disc status (byte 2 bits 1:0) via mos_disc_status_description() — drift-guarded in validate.py.

tracks.description: Last track number in the last session — the track count under MMC's from-1 numbering.

bg_format.description: BG Format Status (byte 7 bits 1:0): the background-format state of DVD+RW/BD-RE/Mount Rainier media. 0 none (not BG-formatted/blank), 1 inactive (started, not running), 2 active (in progress), 3 complete. Values match Linux CDM_MRW_* (cdrom.h).

bg_format_name.description: Stable token for bg_format (mos_bg_format_status_name), null only for an out-of-range code — drift-guarded in validate.py. The in-flight states (inactive/active) signal a disc that may not be reliably readable yet.

disc_structure.description: Disc identity from the Blu-ray Disc Information (DI) structure, read via READ DISC STRUCTURE (0xAD, BD media type, format 0x00) through the ReadDiscStructure convenience method; null for non-BD media (the DI is Blu-ray-only) or when the drive did not return a DI. These are the REGISTERED manufacturer/media-code fields a drive reads to choose its write strategy. mos surfaces them faithfully and does NOT classify: e.g. manufacturer_id 'MILLEN' + media_type_id 'MR1' is Millenniata M-DISC BD, but the MILLEN->M-DISC mapping is the consumer's (same division as MusicBrainz ids). Fields are disc-controlled ASCII, fixed-width with trailing spaces stripped; required-and-nullable (a field empty on the disc reads null).

disc_type.description: Disc Type Identifier (DI offset 8): 'BDR' (BD-R), 'BDW' (BD-RE), 'BDO' (BD-ROM) — the recordable class read from the disc's own structure, independent of the MMC profile.

manufacturer_id.description: Disc Manufacturer ID (DI offset 100, 6 bytes) — the registered mastering/recording manufacturer, e.g. 'MILLEN', 'CMCMAG', 'VERBAT', 'RITEK'.

media_type_id.description: Media Type ID (DI offset 106, 3 bytes), e.g. 'MR1', 'CN2'.

revision.description: Product Revision Number (DI offset 111, 1 byte), e.g. '0'.

physical.description: Physical Format Information from READ DISC STRUCTURE (0xAD, DVD/HD-DVD media type, format 0x00) via the ReadDiscStructure convenience method; null on BD/CD media (this format is the DVD/HD-DVD family) or when the drive did not answer. The disc-reported geometry: book type, layer layout, data-area sector boundaries (end_sector_l0 is the layer break), BCA presence. Numeric fields are the raw spec codes; *_name are the mos token mappings (drift-guarded in validate.py). Offsets per the kernel wire parse (drivers/cdrom/cdrom.c dvd_read_physical).

book_type.description: Book Type (base[0] bits 7:4): 0 DVD-ROM, 2 DVD-R, 0xA DVD+R, 0x4 HD DVD-ROM, ...

book_type_name.description: Stable token for book_type (mos_book_type_name), or null for a code outside the table — consumers fall back to the numeric book_type.

track_path.description: Track path (base[2] bit 4): 'ptp' parallel (single-layer/sequential) or 'otp' opposite.

start_sector.description: Starting Physical Sector Number of the data area (base[5..7], 24-bit).

end_sector.description: End Physical Sector Number of the data area (base[9..11], 24-bit).

end_sector_l0.description: End PSN in layer 0 (base[13..15], 24-bit) — the layer break on dual-layer OTP media; 0 on single-layer.

copyright.description: Copyright Management Information from READ DISC STRUCTURE format 0x01 (DVD/HD-DVD); null on BD/CD media or when not answered. The protection-system type and region mask are surfaced faithfully — mos does NOT classify ('CSS-protected', region semantics are the consumer's), and reads no keys (scope doctrine). Offsets per dvd_read_copyright (cpst buf[4], rmi buf[5]).

protection.description: Copyright Protection System Type (CPST): 0 none, 1 CSS/CPPM, 2 CPRM, 3 AACS.

protection_name.description: Stable token for protection (mos_protection_name), or null for a reserved/unknown code.

region.description: Region Management Information (RMI) mask — the raw byte; region playability is the consumer's interpretation.

volume_name.description: Mounted volume's name (DiskArbitration VolumeName), or null when not mounted or unlabeled. MOUNT-SOURCED ONLY: present-but-unmounted discs read null by design — sector-derived names are the consumer's to obtain and parse (scope doctrine). Volume names are disc-controlled bytes, emitted byte-faithfully under JSON string escaping; terminal quoting is the consumer's job.

cdtext.description: CD-TEXT, read via READ TOC/PMA/ATIP format 0101b through the ReadTableOfContents convenience method; null on non-CD media or a CD that publishes no CD-TEXT. The 'which album is in the drive' disambiguator (album title/performer) plus the per-track song titles (for rip file-naming). SCOPE: the FIRST language block's album Title/Performer and per-track TITLES in single-byte charset — a double-byte (DBCC) field reads null/absent rather than mis-decoded; per-track PERFORMER, the other CD-TEXT field types, and additional language blocks are not decoded (deferred). BEST-EFFORT DISPLAY TEXT, not a fingerprint: audio-CD dedup keys ride on disc.toc, the fail-closed identity primitive. All strings are disc-controlled bytes, emitted byte-faithfully under JSON string escaping; terminal quoting is the consumer's job. Required-and-nullable.

title.description: Album title (CD-TEXT pack type 0x80, track 0, block 0), or null when absent/empty or double-byte.

performer.description: Album performer (CD-TEXT pack type 0x81, track 0, block 0), or null when absent/empty or double-byte.

tracks.description: Per-track CD-TEXT: song title (pack 0x80) and performer (pack 0x81), tracks 1..N, block 0. SPARSE and possibly empty: only tracks carrying a non-empty title OR performer appear, so track numbers may be non-contiguous and the array may be []. Within an entry, title and performer are independently nullable (a various-artists disc may carry a performer but no per-track title, or vice versa).

title.description: Track title, or null when this track carried no (non-empty) title.

performer.description: Track performer, or null when this track carried no (non-empty) performer.

track_info.description: READ TRACK INFORMATION (0x52) for the first track (the track containing LBA 0) via the ReadTrackInformation convenience method — the capacity / append-state surface; null when the drive did not answer. For a single-track pressed DVD/BD, track_size is effectively the disc capacity; for a blank/appendable recordable, next_writable (when not null) is the append point. Offsets per the kernel struct track_information (include/uapi/linux/cdrom.h). next_writable and last_recorded are null when their reply validity bit (NWA_V / LRA_V) is clear — meaningless otherwise.

track_number.description: Track number (byte 2, plus byte 32 MSB on long replies).

track_mode.description: Track mode / Q-channel control nibble (byte 5 bits 3:0).

next_writable.description: Next Writable Address (bytes 12..15), or null when NWA_V (byte 7 bit 0) is clear — the append point on recordable media.

free_blocks.description: Free Blocks remaining in the track (bytes 16..19).

last_recorded.description: Last Recorded Address (bytes 28..31), or null when LRA_V (byte 7 bit 1) is clear.

session_layout.description: Per-session boundaries from the macOS kernel-cached full-TOC (kIOCDMediaTOCKey, the Apple CDTOC blob on the IOCDMedia node) — read with zero SCSI commands and no exclusive access, fresh off the current media node. CD-ONLY (no cached-TOC equivalent exists for DVD/BD): null on non-CD media, or when the IOCDMedia node carries no cached TOC (just-inserted/unrecognized media). This is the richer structure the issued READ TOC format-0000b (`toc` above) does not carry and that disc_info gives only for the LAST session: for each session, the first/last track and the lead-out, so a multi-session disc (e.g. CD-Extra: audio in session 1, a data track in session 2) is resolvable. Decode + cross-check (libcdio read_toc_osx) in SPEC.md.

first_track.description: First track number in the session (POINT 0xA0 PMIN), or null when the session carried no 0xA0 descriptor.

last_track.description: Last track number in the session (POINT 0xA1 PMIN), or null when the session carried no 0xA1 descriptor.

leadout_lba.description: Session lead-out start LBA (POINT 0xA2 MSF, converted minus the 150-frame pregap), or null when the session carried no 0xA2 descriptor.

allOf.title: class is null when profile is null
allOf.description: class is a pure function of profile; a class without a profile would be fabricated data.

allOf.title: volume_name requires a mount
allOf.description: volume_name is DA-sourced and DA carries a name only for mounted volumes; a name with volume_path null would claim a source that cannot have produced it.
